item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"In current SCOPe release 2.08, d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_ are all explicitly classified as domains with SCCS a.298.1.1, the family \"TAL (transcription activator-like) effector\". That family is under superfamily a.298.1 \"TAL effector-like\", fold a.298 \"Left-handed alpha-alpha superhelix\", and class a \"All alpha proteins\". Their very different lengths are expected for TAL effector repeat regions: they are tandem-repeat solenoids, so the same homologous repeat architecture can appear as a short construct, a medium repeat array, or a much longer array. SCOPe sequence records give d2kq5a_ as 51 aa from PthA, d3v6pa_ as 373 aa from dHax3, and d4cj9a_ as 752 aa from BurrH; the PDB metadata describes 2kq5 as a 1.5-repeat section of PthA, 3v6p as an 11-tandem-repeat DNA-binding domain of dHax3, and 4cj9 as BurrH DNA-binding protein. Thus the family assignment is about shared evolutionary/structural repeat architecture, not equal total sequence length.
